- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to mean-revert — add a slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to counteract downward momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates short-term volatility in sentiment-heavy periods — increase forecast variance by 0.3–0.8% for 3–7 day horizons.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag — delay downward corrections by 1–2 days and add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid premature sell-off.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean reversion — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is weak or negative over last 5–7 days.
